title: Composite Cascade Boxes for the Thrust Reverser on VDK-56B Powered Aircraft
abstract: Proposal to replace the cast aluminium thrust reverser cascade boxes with injection-moulded composite items, saving weight per engine position and removing a repair scheme that overhaul shops increasingly decline to carry out.

sections.reason: Cast aluminium cascade boxes are damaged by ingested debris and by the fan cowl support strut during removal, and the published weld repair for a cracked vane is now declined by three of the five approved shops because the fixture is out of production. The result is that a damaged box is scrapped, and box scrappage has become the largest single line in the thrust reverser overhaul bill. Sixty-one boxes were scrapped across the tracked fleet last year against fourteen repaired. There is also a weight case: the composite item is appreciably lighter and the change contributes to the family weight reduction target.
sections.description: The cast aluminium boxes are replaced by injection-moulded glass-reinforced polyetherimide items of identical vane geometry and external interface, so no change is needed to the translating sleeve or the blocker doors. The vendor clamp kit ASH774095-25 is retained at the forward attachment and the firewall panel D7830136178554 is renewed because the composite box needs a wider land at the aft edge. The cascade FINs 4017ET and 699ET keep their positions; the thrust reverser clamp FIN 47ET1 is disturbed during removal and is renewed as a matter of course. The change is done with the reverser halves removed and on a stand, from zones 472, 474, 481 and 483. Drawing D78300079325 issue D carries the box interface and the attachment torque values.
sections.effects: Estimated mass reduction of 6.2 kg per engine position, symmetric between engines. No electrical load change. The composite box is fully interchangeable with the aluminium item at box level and the two may be mixed within one reverser half, which matters because operators will convert on attrition rather than as a campaign. Thrust reverser performance is unchanged at the certified setting but the reverse thrust demonstration must be repeated because the vane surface finish differs. The weld repair scheme in the component manual is deleted and replaced by a scrap-and-replace policy with a lower unit cost.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must confirm that the reverse thrust demonstration can be done on the ground rather than in flight, whether the composite box survives the fire test required for its position, and whether the aft firewall panel change forces a nacelle structure modification that has not been costed.

type_data.balance_impact: Symmetric between engine positions, no measurable effect
type_data.production_impact: Production cut-in not proposed at this stage; the VDK-56B nacelle is out of production
